title: Weekly cetuximab

agents.name: Cetuximab
agents.mechanism: Blocks growth messages at the cell surface
agents.explanation: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks growth messages. In bowel cancer, a validated RAS wild-type result helps identify whether this approach is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care.
agents.watch: Report rash or sore nails early. Tell the nurse immediately about infusion symptoms. Eye pain, new breathing problems or severe diarrhoea need prompt advice. Blood tests check minerals during treatment and for two months afterwards.
risks: Rash, dry skin, cracks and sore nails
Infusion reaction; rare serious lung or skin effects

questions.a: Cetuximab alone is an option for RAS wild-type bowel cancer that has spread after oxaliplatin and irinotecan have failed, when irinotecan cannot be tolerated. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates to understand the cycle?
questions.a: No. The graph explains a general pattern. Your hospital arranges appointments; the guide and its safety information are available without entering anything.

questions.q: Will I have a pump at home?
questions.a: There is no home fluorouracil pump in this regimen. Your team chooses a cannula or central line based on your veins and wider treatment plan.

questions.q: What happens if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team checks the cause and may delay, reduce, change or stop one medicine. Ask which component changes and when you should next attend; do not restart yourself.

questions.q: How will I know whether it is helping?
questions.a: Scans, symptoms and clinical review assess benefit. A rash, side effect or good day alone cannot show whether the cancer is responding.
The graphic below shows the relationship.

questions.q: What about fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding?
questions.a: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.
RAS testing selects cetuximab treatment in colorectal cancer. Confirm the cancer-specific plan with your team.

questions.q: Which checks continue when treatment changes or finishes?
questions.a: Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last cetuximab dose; assign responsibility before treatment ends.

phases_note: This is a general explanation, not an appointment calendar. Delays or changes are decided by your team. Each medicine can need a different change.
timeline_note: NCCP defines the treatment days. Symptom bands are broad educational guidance; reactions can occur on any day, and cumulative effects may continue between cycles.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell require immediate contact. Serious symptoms override any timeline or diary.
teachback: Can you explain which visits are planned, whether a pump is involved, and which symptoms mean you should call today? No dates or symptom scores are needed to use this guide.
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, serious and lasting risks, fertility/pregnancy precautions and the contact plan. Confirm RAS selection for colorectal treatment, infusion premedication, skin care and post-treatment mineral checks. Discuss severe or delayed infusion reactions and the agreed observation plan; a previous severe cetuximab reaction must be reported even after recovery.
urgent_extra: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly.

chapters.intro: The setting changes what benefit means.

items.title: Why this option?
items.text: Cetuximab alone is an option for RAS wild-type bowel cancer that has spread after oxaliplatin and irinotecan have failed, when irinotecan cannot be tolerated. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

items.title: A plan that can change
items.text: For bowel cancer, discuss control of cancer and symptoms, and whether further local treatment may become possible. Your preferences and priorities matter.

items.title: Blood tests and medicines
items.text: Review blood counts, kidney/liver tests, symptoms, allergies and all medicines and supplements.  Tell the team about red-meat allergy or tick bites before cetuximab because these can be associated with infusion-reaction risk.

items.title: Preparing access
items.text: Allow for blood tests, review, pharmacy preparation, infusion and observation. A port is not automatically required; ask which access is suitable.

chapters.title: Symptoms in context
chapters.intro: Report what changed and how it affects you.

items.title: When to call
items.text: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly.

items.title: Bowel symptoms
items.text: Follow your written rescue plan. Fever, blood, severe pain, reduced urine or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

items.title: Skin and nail changes
items.text: Start the prescribed skin-care plan early, use moisturiser and sun protection, and report painful or infected skin or nails. Keep mineral blood-test appointments during treatment and for two months after cetuximab.

items.title: Food, activity and practical help
items.text: Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines, pace activities and ask for nutritional, emotional or practical support.

items.title: Pregnancy and fertility
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.

chapters.title: Visits and treatment sequence
chapters.intro: Know which steps happen in the clinic and at home.

items.title: The exact delivery plan
items.text: Cetuximab on Day 1. No home chemotherapy pump. A repeating 7-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan.

items.title: Symptoms and monitoring
items.text: Continue the cetuximab skin plan and mineral checks for two months after the last dose. Ask which medicines to continue, when to seek help and how response will be assessed.

items.title: Next decisions
items.text: The team reviews benefit, side effects and your priorities. Supportive and palliative care can help alongside active treatment. Ask for a clear next-step and contact plan.

day_groups.title: Treatment and checks
day_groups.body: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and your prescription before treatment. Premedicines and observation are part of cetuximab visits.
day_groups.action: Know the contact number and the next planned visit.

day_groups.title: Care between visits
day_groups.body: Follow the skin-care or bowel-symptom plan provided. There is no pump to remove.
day_groups.action: Call early for symptoms; do not wait for the next appointment.

day_groups.title: Recovery and the next review
day_groups.body: The team uses symptoms, tests and your priorities to decide what happens next.
day_groups.action: Bring questions and a symptom record if useful; this is optional.

support.title: First cetuximab dose
support.text: Skin care and sun protection under local EGFR policy. Premedicines and monitoring add time to every cetuximab visit. Your team will confirm the observation period before you leave; do not assume that later visits can omit observation. Report delayed reaction symptoms urgently. Monthly electrolytes/Mg/Ca for two months after last dose.

support.title: Subsequent weekly cetuximab
support.text: Premedication continues for subsequent infusions. Post-treatment monthly electrolytes/Mg/Ca for two months.

support.title: Previous infusion reactions
support.text: Tell the team about any previous severe antibody reaction, even if you feel well now. Premedication does not remove all reaction risk. Report breathing problems, swelling, faintness or rapidly worsening symptoms immediately.

evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: In selected previously treated bowel cancer, cetuximab improved disease control and survival compared with supportive care.
evidence.interpretation: In selected previously treated bowel cancer, cetuximab improved disease control and survival compared with supportive care.
evidence.population: Previously treated KRAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer.

chronology_notes.title: Your planned visits
chronology_notes.text: Cetuximab on Day 1. No home chemotherapy pump. A repeating 7-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan.

chronology_notes.title: No guaranteed safe days
chronology_notes.text: An infection, reaction or other urgent problem can occur at any time. The graph does not predict a personal low point.

chronology_notes.title: Care continues
chronology_notes.text: Continue the skin-care plan and mineral checks arranged after cetuximab. Ask which medicines to continue and when your next review is planned.

steps.title: Before treatment
steps.text: Confirm tests, medicines and the exact schedule.

steps.title: Prepare for the visit
steps.text: Arrange transport if premedicines or symptoms affect driving.

steps.title: At the day ward
steps.text: Blood results, symptoms and venous access are checked.

steps.title: Infusion and observation
steps.text: The first cetuximab infusion is usually about two hours and later weekly infusions about one hour. Premedicines and monitoring add time to every cetuximab visit. Your team will confirm the observation period before you leave; do not assume that later visits can omit observation.

steps.title: At home
steps.text: Follow the skin-care and/or bowel plan. There is no pump to disconnect.

steps.title: Next review
steps.text: Confirm the next appointment and follow-up tests.

details.title: Do I need a port?
details.text: A peripheral cannula or existing central line may be used. A port is not automatically needed; the team considers your veins and overall treatment plan.

details.title: If the schedule changes
details.text: Ask the unit to confirm the next visit and which medicine is being changed. Do not copy dates from another regimen.

details.title: Observation at every antibody visit
details.text: Premedicines and monitoring add time to every cetuximab visit. Your team will confirm the observation period before you leave; do not assume that later visits can omit observation.

sections.title: Treatment phases and appointments
sections.text: One larger first infusion is followed by weekly infusions. Bowel-cancer treatment continues while helping and tolerated.

sections.title: Access and practical support

indication_text: EGFR-expressing RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer after the specified previous therapies
administration_text: The first infusion usually takes two hours and later infusions one hour. Extra observation is needed after the first two infusions. There is no home chemotherapy pump.
monitoring_summary: Before starting and regularly during treatment: blood count, kidney and liver tests; confirm RAS, EGFR and previous treatment suitability. Review skin, nails, eyes, breathing and mineral levels. Premedicines and monitoring add time to every cetuximab visit. Your team will confirm the observation period before you leave; do not assume that later visits can omit observation. Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last cetuximab. Scans and recovery checks follow the consultant plan.
